newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: KEDO decides not to award Nov fuel import tender.
newsitem.headline: KEDO decides not to award Nov fuel import tender.

text.p: The Korean Peninsular Energy Development (KEDO) has decided not to award its tender to buy fuel oil for November delivery, traders said on Wednesday.
"KEDO just said that there is no award, and gave us no reasons," a South Korean trader told Reuters.
KEDO's tender to buy 42,000 tonnes of 2.0-percent sulphur grade heavy residual fuel oil for delivery between November 10 and 29, was originally scheduled to close on November 6.
Its validity was extended from November 7 to November 8.
Traders said the decision not to award the tender might be linked to talks that the market was nervous about a recent threat by North Korea to spurn peace talks proposed by Seoul and Washington.

According to news reports, the threat highlighted a new obstacle in the already difficult task of trying to lure Pyongyang into talks to end an armed truce with Seoul dating from the 1950-1953 Korean War.

South Korea has insisted talks cannot resume unless North Korea apologises over a September submarine incursion into the South and it has withdrawn past offers to brief North Korea on the talks along with the U.S.
U.S. officials have indicated they support Seoul's position.
On Monday, the North Korean foreign ministry accused Washington of backing away from four-way peace talks, including China, proposed by the U.S. and South Korea.

Pyongyang has said that the U.S. refusal to make a 'joint explanation' means there is some change in its position, referring to the proposed briefing. Pyongyang sees this as a revocation of the four-way talks, a North Korean official said.
KEDO, an international organisation established to implement nuclear non-proliferation in North Korea, has agreed to supply the country with 500,000 tonnes of fuel oil annually.
